title: Designing Your Network Architecture 📐
description: Guidelines for choosing the number of layers, neurons, and connections.

slides.title: No Magic Formula ✨
slides.content:
# Architecture is Part Art, Part Science

Key hyperparameters:
- Number of hidden layers
- Number of neurons per layer
- Type of activation

Start simple, then increase complexity only if needed.

> Analogy: Building a bridge – you need enough supports to carry the load, but too many add cost and may cause instability.

slides.title: Input & Output Dimensions 📏
slides.content:
# Input Shape
Must match your data features. Example: 28×28 image → `input_shape=(784,)` after flatten.

# Output Shape
- Regression (predict a number): 1 unit, no activation (or linear).
- Binary classification: 1 unit, sigmoid.
- Multi‑class classification: number of classes units, softmax.

quizData.question: For a model predicting house price, what output layer is appropriate?
quizData.explanation: Regression needs a linear output (no activation) to predict any continuous value.

slides.title: Hidden Layers & Width 📐
slides.content:
# How Many Layers / Neurons?
- 1‑2 hidden layers solve many simple problems.
- More layers can model more complex patterns, but risk overfitting.
- Typical widths: powers of 2 (32, 64, 128).

**Rule of thumb:** start with one hidden layer with `n` neurons (where n = number of input features) and adjust.

slides.title: Start Small, Iterate 🐢
slides.content: Avoid creating a giant network from the start. It wastes time and can overfit. Build a minimal working model, then gradually increase complexity while monitoring validation loss.
